slides.title: Red-black rules
slides.sub: Color is one bit per node
slides.main: The root is black, no two reds in a row, black height is equal on all paths.

captions: Every node is red or black; empty links are black leaves
Rule 1: the root is black
Rule 2: a red node has two black children, so no red-red
Rule 3: every downward path has the same number of black nodes (black height)

slides.title: Why logarithmic
slides.main: Height ≤ 2 log₂(n + 1): reds fit one at a time between blacks.

captions: The shortest path is all black nodes: say b of them
Any path has the same b blacks, and reds never touch, so at most b reds between them
The long path is at most twice the short one: height ≤ 2 log₂(n + 1)

slides.title: Insert
slides.main: A violation needs a red parent; then the uncle decides.

captions: Insert 11 as in a plain search tree: right child of node 10
Color the new node red: black heights stay the same
Parent 10 is red: the no-red-red rule is broken; grandparent 12 must be black
The uncle, the parent's sibling, decides: here it is 14, red

slides.title: Red uncle
slides.main: Parent and uncle turn black, grandparent turns red: no rotations, the problem may move up.

captions: Parent 10 and uncle 14 are red, grandparent 12 is black
Parent and uncle become black, grandparent red: black heights unchanged, no rotations
The grandparent's parent 8 is black, so all is fine. Otherwise we would repeat for the grandparent

slides.title: Black uncle
slides.main: Kink: rotate the parent; line: rotate the grandparent and recolor. At most two rotations.

captions: The uncle is black (empty). Node 4 is the right child of left parent 3: a kink
Left rotation around 3: the kink became a line (4 above 3)
Now node, parent and grandparent form one line
Right rotation of grandparent 5 and recoloring: 4 is the black root, 3 and 5 are red children

slides.title: Deletion
slides.main: Fixed by the sibling's color; at most three rotations.

captions: A node with two children is replaced by its successor; we delete a node with ≤ 1 child
A deleted black node removes a black from the path: the "double black" must be resolved
Red sibling: a rotation turns it into the black sibling case
Black sibling: red nephew means rotations; black nephews mean recolor and move up. At most three rotations

slides.title: AVL or red-black
slides.main: AVL searches faster, red-black updates faster; both are O(log n).

captions: AVL is stricter: a slightly shorter tree
So reading from AVL is a bit faster
Insertion: up to two rotations in both
Deletion is cheaper in red-black. All operations are O(log n) in the worst case

slides.title: Checking invariants
slides.sub: Tests that catch bugs at once
slides.main: Check order, colors and black height after every operation.

captions: After each operation, make sure the traversal is increasing
The root is black
A red node has no red children
All paths have equal black height. Checking after every insert catches a bug at once
